conversation.content:
Hello, I’m so glad you’re here. My name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician—my whole job is helping new moms sort through the emotional ups and downs that can come after a baby arrives. I’ll be guiding you through a quick, well-trusted questionnaire called the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale**—EPDS for short. It’s simply 10 questions about how you’ve been feeling over the past seven days; it isn’t a test or a judgment, just a snapshot that helps us figure out the best way to support you right now.

Everything we talk about stays between you, me, and the clinical team. You can answer as briefly or as fully as you like, and if anything feels uncomfortable, just let me know. Ready to begin?

1. In the past week, how often have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

I’ve still been able to laugh—maybe not as easily as before the baby, but when my partner makes a silly face or when the dog does something goofy, I definitely chuckle. I’d say most days I find at least one thing to laugh about.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Yeah, like I said, I can still laugh—maybe not quite as hard or as often, but I do find things funny most days.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things
I still look forward to little things—like my morning coffee or taking the baby out in the stroller when it’s sunny. They’re small, but they feel good.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong
Not really. If the baby’s fussy or I’m running late, I might think “ugh, I should’ve done that differently,” but I don’t stay stuck on it. I shrug it off pretty quickly.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Sometimes I get a sudden “what if something’s wrong with the baby?” feeling, even when everything looks fine. It doesn’t last long and I can usually talk myself down, but it pops up out of nowhere maybe every other day.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason
No, I haven’t felt that kind of panic—just the little worries I mentioned, nothing that makes my heart race or feels like a real fright.
Things have been getting on top of me

Now and then, when the baby’s having a rough night or the laundry piles up, I feel a bit swamped, but it passes once I tick a couple jobs off the list. Most days I feel like I’m keeping my head above water.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping
No, my sleep’s actually been okay. I crash pretty quickly once the baby settles, and I don’t lie there feeling upset or anything.
I have felt sad or miserable
I wouldn’t say I feel sad or miserable. Tired, sure, but my mood’s pretty steady—no gloom hanging over me.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying
I really haven’t cried much at all—maybe once when I was extra tired, but that was more frustration than unhappiness, and it was over in a minute.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, never. That hasn’t crossed my mind.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 5: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Date: [today]

Source: 10-item Edinburgh-based self-report; responses reviewed line-by-line.

Areas endorsed (frequency & intensity sub-clinical):
• Occasional, transient “what-if” worries about infant safety without persistent anxious arousal
• Mild, situational overwhelm relieved by task completion; no persistent sense of inadequacy or hopelessness

Areas not endorsed:
• Anhedonia, sustained low mood, crying spells, sleep disruption secondary to mood, guilt/self-blame, panic symptoms, self-harm ideas

Pattern summary:
Patient retains capacity for pleasure, humour, and forward-looking enjoyment. No evidence of sustained depressive or anxiety symptoms meeting screening threshold for major postpartum depression or anxiety disorder. No current safety concerns.

Risk level: Low (routine psycho-education and standard postpartum follow-up recommended).
